review.title: Review
review.description: Spaced review is what keeps what you learned yours. Here is what is due, what is coming, and what you keep forgetting.
review.dueCount: {n, plural, one {# review due} other {# reviews due}}
review.emptyWhy: Come back when something falls due. Reviewing early does not help it stick.
review.overdueWarning: {n, plural, one {# is overdue} other {# are overdue}} — past the day the interval was meant to end.
review.upcomingHelp: Scheduled cards, not a prediction of how you will do.
review.upcomingEmpty: Nothing scheduled yet. Cards come from what you miss and what you study.
review.originHelp: No card shows up here at random — each one has an origin.

kinds.posicao-exataHelp: A puzzle you did not solve, or solved with a hint.
kinds.erro-de-partidaHelp: A move you actually played that the engine flagged.
kinds.finalHelp: A position from an endgame lesson you studied.
kinds.conceitoHelp: Curriculum: only what you have already been taught lands here.
kinds.repertorioHelp: The move you yourself chose for your line.

review.lapsingHelp: You have forgotten these more than once. That is not failure: it is the sign the idea deserves a lesson again, not another attempt.
review.lapsingEmpty: Nothing slipping. What you reviewed has been holding.
review.historyHelp: Your latest sessions, and how each one ended.
review.historyEmpty: No reviews yet. The first one shows up as soon as a card falls due.
review.howBody: Trying before you see the answer is what makes it stick — that is why the solution comes last. Reviewing early does not help: the interval exists so you almost forget. And missing one never demotes what you already learned; what changes is when that card comes back.
review.sessionDescription: Review starts with what is due. Try before you see the answer: recall is what fixes it.
